title: Last call for Amazon UK's top Black Friday deals: flagships, foldables, mid-rangers and more
author: Peter
body_paragraphs: The week of sales preceding Black Friday is coming to an end – but you still have enough time to pick up a new smartphone on sale. In fact, the prices of several models have gone down since the sales started. The prices of foldables in particular have seen notable downward corrections since last week – for example, a 12/512GB Galaxy Z Fold8 was £1,600 last week and is £1,400 now.
Some of the non-folding phones got cheaper too. Most models are still in stock, but a few are no longer available, e.g. the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max and the Sony Xperia 1 VIII.

The Oppo Find X10 series and the Xiaomi 18 Pro series are in competition for being some of the best flagships of 2026 and their excellent cameras are a big part of that. Check out their reviews for an in-depth look at the phones and their many excellent qualities. The Find X10 Pro Max is out of stock now, has been for a few days and will probably not be restocked before the sales event ends.
Do note that the Xiaomi 18 Pro offer requires a Prime subscription (£9 a month or you can use the free trial).

These flagships have capable cameras too, but they aren’t quite as obsessed as the group above and their prices are noticeably lower. Samsung Galaxy S26 and Google Pixel 11 Pro models offer size variety, while the Poco F9 Ultra and F9 Pro are the value-for-money flagships.

The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 with 512GB of storage now costs £200 less than it did last week. The base 256GB variant is only £20 cheaper, though. The book-style competition dropped too – the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra 256GB is now £50 less than it was a week ago, while the Motorola Razr Fold is £60 less.

Similarly, the Galaxy Z Flip8 price took a significant tumble – it was £1,220 last week and it now goes for £950. The base 256GB model dropped by £50. The Motorola Razr 70 is £70 cheaper than it was a week ago.

The Z Fold8 Ultra finally upgraded the battery capacity, but if you want a 215g / 8.9mm foldable with a 200MP main camera, the older Z Fold7 is still a solid pick – and it costs £100 less than it did a week ago. Meanwhile, flip foldables evolve even slower, so the Z Flip7 offers a very similar experience to the Z Flip8.

The categories above already have several 6.3” entries from Samsung and Google, but here are a few more. These vary in capabilities quite a bit, but you can get a telephoto camera (Oppo Reno16) or a surprisingly large 6,330mAh battery (Poco X8s) in this category.

Removing the size restriction, here are some more premium phones – these sit between mid-rangers and flagships both in terms of capabilities and price. The Honor 600 Pro offers a 200MP main camera, a 50MP 3.5x telephoto camera and a Snapdragon 8 Elite chipset. The Xiaomi 17T and 17T Pro also have 50MP telephoto modules with longer 5x lenses, plus a Dimensity 8500 Ultra and Dimensity 9500, respectively.
The Redmi Note 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max don’t have the 200MP cameras of their predecessors, but they have huge 8,340mAh and 9,210mAh batteries with 67W and 100W fast charging, respectively.
